title.narrative: Integrated GBV and CP response to those affected by protection-related risk from El Nino-induced floods in North Galkacyo Puntland State.

description.narrative: ltpgtPMWDO will provide CP and GBV case management (and referral based on informed consent)for up to 360 children ( up to 50% to be girls) and 540 survivors (280 women, 240 girls while men and boys anticipated to be up to 20 survivors relative to previous prevalence and reporting trends). To address the multisectorial approach referral within case management process will be initiated in line with the SOP. The project will ensure compassionate, age-appropriate services including Psychosocial support services and psychological First Aid within the existing community protection desks, at one-stop center (OSC), in women and girls’ safe spaces (WGSS), and child-friendly spaces with trained CP / GBV case workers, who based on need will provide both static and mobile response in line with internal activity roster/assignment. PMWDO will at the onset organize orientation for case workers refresher training with an emphasis on Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE) and GBV in an emergency (to improve quality of service delivery by mobile teams), and preposition resources to support the transport for Survivors to access Clinical management of Rape services (as well as capacity building on CMR to health care providers) as part of essential services for the recovery of survivors of GBV within case management process for medical support.ltbrgtThe trained caseworkers will support the Identification, tracing, and re-unification of up to 360 Unaccompanied and Separated Children (estimating 50% to be girls), while also accessing and linking to appropriate, alternative care during tracing or when family tracing is not possible and it is in line with the CM SoP as well as Child Protection Minimum standard on the best interest of the children will be applied. The mobile teams will strengthen existing service delivery points including safe spaces for children /Child-Friendly Spaces (CFS), and protection desks by supporting inclusive approaches for 1,200 participants (200 women, 400 girls, 400 boys, and 200 men) that are contextually appropriate based on positive social and cultural activities that promote the ability to function in other areas of their lives. Widely provide Awareness on prevention best practices and information on the updated service mappings (reaching up to 3,000 participants). Engage with 1,200 children for access to PSS kits in distress in Child-Friendly Space within a protected environment that can promote play and development. lt/pgtltpgtPMWDO will provide Case management during and Referral to access clinical management of rape services for survivors of GBV including medical treatment for IPV. The case workers will provide transport cost for 320 GBV survivors to access CMR services within different health facilities in-line with WHO CMR guidelines and adherence to ethical standards which improves referral mechanisms for survivors, and encourage the survivors to report on time within the protocols available for 72 hours and 120 hours (in line with relevant protocols). Identify most vulnerable Survivors based on set criteria for Disbursement of Unconditional Cash/voucher assistance support as mitigation for GBV. Provision of cash voucher assistance to 320 vulnerable women and girls to prevent GBV incidences from taking place and reducing the level of risk by decreasing the person’s level of exposure to a threat, reducing vulnerabilities, and enhancing individual capacities and there after conduct Posr Distribution Monitoring on items Distributed including Cash, (PSS and Dignity) Kits. In the GBV Stop Center (OSC) in Galkacyo districts by using the global standard guidelines for establishing Women and Girls Safe Space Place (WGSS), PMWDO will support based on both static and mobile teams as well as link to other sectors through referrals based on informed consent. Dignity kits will be provided to GBV survivors and vulnerable women (up to 600 women and 400 girls) and awareness on both CP and GBV in the target communities in North Galkayo ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
